family_title_en: Is the syllable open or closed?

stages.ix_title: Is the syllable open or closed?

prompt.en: Is this syllable open or closed?
prompt.ko: 이 음절은 열린 음절인가요, 닫힌 음절인가요?

what_to_do.ko: 열린 음절 또는 닫힌 음절을 누르세요.

gold_items.stem: The part pen in the word open
The part by in the word baby

roots: Keep the two labels open then closed. Never change the words, the order, or the count.
A one-word stem is the syllable to judge. In a longer stem, the named part must be a real syllable of that word, and you judge only that part.
An open syllable ends in one vowel letter, and a final y counts as a vowel. A closed syllable ends in a consonant. Use one vowel, and a blend or digraph may sit beside it.
Do not target silent-e words, vowel-team syllables, or a consonant-le part. Those are other syllable types.
Use real spellings. Skip misspelled wordlist lines. Use school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather words. No brands or real names.
Keep about half the answers open and half closed. Tier 3 uses a final y or a closed part inside a misleading word.

tier_rules.1: One-word stems only, each a real word a child knows. Open ends in a, e, i, o, or u. Closed ends in a consonant after one vowel. No final y on tier 1.
tier_rules.2: Five-word stems that name one part of a two-syllable word. The part has one vowel and is clearly open or clearly closed.
tier_rules.3: Longer stems of about seven words. Use a closed part inside a word such as open, or an open part that ends with the vowel letter y.

open.en: This syllable ends with a vowel, so it is open.
open.ko: 이 음절은 모음으로 끝나서 열린 음절입니다.

closed.en: This syllable ends with a consonant, so it is closed.
closed.ko: 이 음절은 자음으로 끝나서 닫힌 음절입니다.

open_y.en: Y is a vowel here. It ends with a vowel, so it is open.
open_y.ko: 여기서 y는 모음입니다. 모음으로 끝나서 열린 음절입니다.

closed_part.en: Look at that part only. It ends with a consonant, so it is closed.
closed_part.ko: 그 부분만 보세요. 자음으로 끝나서 닫힌 음절입니다.
